question: Where can I access healthcare in Kakuma?
answer: Health services in Kakuma are provided free of charge through UNHCR and its health partners at the camp health facilities. For non-emergencies, visit the nearest health post during opening hours. For emergencies, go to the nearest health facility immediately or ask any staff member to help you reach emergency care. Bring your refugee ID or registration document when you visit.

question: How can I get maternal or antenatal care in Kakuma?
answer: Pregnant women can receive antenatal and maternal care at the maternal health services in the camp, provided by UNHCR health partners. Ask at any health post to be directed to the maternal health point, and carry your registration document.

question: Where can I get legal assistance in Kakuma?
answer: Legal assistance and protection support are available through UNHCR and its protection partners in Kakuma. Visit the protection or legal aid desk at the service point, where you can get help with your case, rights, and referrals. If you feel unsafe, tell a protection officer immediately.

question: How do I register as an asylum seeker in Kenya?
answer: Asylum seekers in Kenya register with the Department of Refugee Services (DRS) and UNHCR. Registration, asylum procedures, and documentation are handled at the designated registration office. Visit the DRS office in Kakuma or the registration point at the service centre to start or continue your registration.

question: How can I request an interpreter in Kakuma?
answer: Interpretation support is available free of charge to help you access services. Ask any staff member at the service desk to arrange an interpreter for your appointment, and let them know your preferred language. Do not let a language barrier stop you from getting help.

question: I received a document I do not understand. What should I do?
answer: If you receive a document you do not understand, you can bring it to the service point in Kakuma and ask a staff member to explain it. You can also use the SemaSasa document scanner to extract and translate the text, then ask staff to confirm any actions or deadlines it mentions.

question: How do I register as a refugee in Bidibidi?
answer: Refugee registration in Uganda is carried out by the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) together with UNHCR. Registration, documentation, and birth registration are handled at the settlement registration point. Visit the OPM or UNHCR registration desk in Bidibidi to begin the process.
organisation: Office of the Prime Minister (OPM) / UNHCR

question: How can I request an interpreter in Bidibidi?
answer: Interpretation support is available to help you communicate with service providers. Ask staff at the service point to arrange an interpreter and tell them your preferred language, so you can be understood during your appointment.

question: How do I give feedback or ask for help from organisations in Bidibidi?
answer: You can reach organisations working in Bidibidi through the inter-agency feedback, referral and resolution mechanism (FRRM). Use it to request assistance, ask questions, or report a concern, and you will be directed to the right partner organisation.
source_title: Feedback and Referral Mechanism - UNHCR Help Uganda

question: How do I receive cash assistance (CBI) in Kakuma?
answer: Cash assistance from UNHCR is delivered through a bank account. Most Kakuma camp refugees are paid via KCB Bank, and Kalobeyei residents via Equity Bank. Each household gets one free ATM card in the name of its focal point. All UNHCR services are free — you should never pay anyone to receive your assistance.

question: I lost my ATM card or did not receive my cash. What should I do?
answer: Report a lost, stolen or damaged ATM card to KCB or Equity Bank immediately; a replacement costs KES 500. Never share your PIN with anyone. For problems with your cash assistance, visit a UNHCR field post or call the free national helpline 1517. Paying anyone to fix it is fraud — report it to UNHCR.

question: How do I get a birth certificate in Kakuma?
answer: Birth certificates are issued by the Civil Registrar in Lodwar, with monthly registration missions at UNHCR Field Posts 1 and 4 and in Kalobeyei. Bring the birth notification (pink slip) and your proof of registration. Children born in Kenya or to at least one Kenyan parent are eligible.

question: How do I get a movement pass to travel from Kakuma?
answer: Movement passes are issued by the Camp Manager at Field Posts 1, 2 and 4 and in Kalobeyei, Monday to Friday from 9 AM to 3 PM. Processing takes about 2 to 3 days.

question: I lost my refugee document. What should I do?
answer: If you lose a document, first report it to the police and obtain a Police Abstract, then inform UNHCR so they can liaise with Civil Registration to help you replace it.

question: How does the refugee status (RSD) interview and decision process work in Kakuma?
answer: Refugee Status Determination is handled at the DRS Data and Processing Centre in Kakuma 4, next to the Kakuma 4 police post. Interviews are held Tuesday to Thursday and you are notified of your date by phone call and SMS. Decision letters are given out on Fridays. If your claim is rejected, you can appeal to the Refugee Appeals Board within 30 days; the Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK) can help you file the appeal.
source_title: Refugee Status Determination - UNHCR Help Kenya (Kakuma)

question: Who provides free legal help in Bidibidi and how do I reach them?
answer: In Bidibidi, free legal assistance is provided by the International Rescue Committee (IRC). Services include legal counselling, information on Ugandan law, and help accessing the courts — all free of charge. For complaints, call the toll-free FRRM helpline 0800 32 32 32. In an emergency, call 999 or 112.

question: How do I access health care and emergencies in Bidibidi?
answer: In Bidibidi, health services are provided by the International Rescue Committee (IRC) at government and UNHCR-partner facilities, mostly free of charge and shared with the host community. For an emergency, contact your nearest Village Health Team (VHT) member by phone or in person; ambulances are sent for critical cases to the nearest health centre, with referral to district or regional hospitals if needed. For complaints, call the toll-free FRRM helpline 0800 32 32 32.

question: I have experienced gender-based violence. Where can I get help in Kakuma?
answer: In Kakuma, survivors of gender-based violence can get free, confidential help from the Danish Refugee Council (DRC). Call the toll-free helpline 0800720414 (7 days a week) or WhatsApp 0715573845, or visit the nearest DRC field office or UNHCR field post. Support includes case management, psychosocial support, and referral to medical care (ideally within 72 hours), to police, and to legal partners. To report a crime, go to the nearest police station; a female officer is available at Kakuma Main Police Station.
source_title: Sexual and Gender-Based Violence - UNHCR Help Kenya (Kakuma)

question: How do I report that a child is unaccompanied or at risk in Kakuma?
answer: In Kakuma, child protection services are provided by the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and, in Kalobeyei, by Terre des Hommes (TDH). To report a child who is unaccompanied, separated, or at risk, call the toll-free lines DRC 0800720414 or TDH 0800721774, or contact UNHCR directly. Child-friendly Furaha Centres offer play activities and case management.

question: Where can I get mental health or counselling support in Kakuma?
answer: Mental health and psychosocial support is available free at health facilities across Kakuma and Kalobeyei, including counselling, psychotherapy, and medication. Providers include AIC (toll-free 0800720845), IRC (0800720605), and DRC (0800720414); specialised trauma support is offered by CVT and IsraAid (0712827444). Ask at any health centre to be referred.
source_title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support - UNHCR Help Kenya (Kakuma)

question: How do I register the birth of my baby in the settlement?
answer: Birth registration is free. First get the birth notification: from the health centre if the baby was born there, or record it with your local leaders and have it stamped by the sub-county if born elsewhere. Then take the notification and the baby to the OPM and UNHCR registration desk to add the child to your family attestation. Get a short birth certificate from your sub-county, then a long birth certificate from NIRA using the short certificate and the notification.

question: I have experienced gender-based violence. Where can I get help in Bidibidi?
answer: In Bidibidi, survivors of gender-based violence can get free, confidential support from TPO Uganda. Help includes immediate medical care (for rape survivors: PEP against HIV, STI prophylaxis, and emergency contraception), counselling and clinical mental health care, legal assistance, and safe shelter or relocation when needed. Call the toll-free FRRM helpline 0800 32 32 32 or email protection@unhcr.org.

question: How do I report an unaccompanied or at-risk child in Bidibidi?
answer: In Bidibidi, child protection is provided by UNHCR together with IRC and World Vision. Support includes individual help for at-risk or separated children, family tracing and reunification, alternative care for unaccompanied or separated children, and referrals to psychosocial and medical care. To report a concern, call the toll-free helpline 0800 32 32 32. All services are free.

question: What basic support (food, shelter, water, household items) do I get as a new refugee in the settlement?
answer: New refugees in the settlements receive emergency shelter kits and non-food items such as blankets, sleeping mats, jerrycans, basins, soap and sanitary napkins. The World Food Programme (WFP) provides food assistance as cash or food; call the WFP helpline 0800210210 or 0800323232. Safe water is provided and emergency latrines are set up within 72 hours of arrival. Registered refugees also receive solar lanterns and regular soap and hygiene distributions. All UNHCR and partner services are free; for complaints call the FRRM helpline 0800 32 32 32.
source_title: Support in the Settlements - UNHCR Help Uganda

question: What number do I call for an ambulance or medical emergency in Kakuma?
answer: Only call an ambulance for a life-saving emergency. In Kakuma 1, call 0719105775 (IRC). In Kakuma 2, 3 and 4, call 0719105549 (IRC). In Kalobeyei, call 0707173515 (KRCS).

question: Which hospitals and health centres can I go to in Kakuma, and when are they open?
answer: Ammusait General Hospital (Clinic 7) in Kakuma 4 and Kaapoka Health Centre in Kakuma 1, both run by IRC, are open 24 hours. Natukubenyo Health Centre in Kalobeyei Village 1 (KRCS) is also open 24 hours. Dispensaries and clinics open 8am to 3pm. The general hospital offers in-patient care, a surgery theatre and imaging (ultrasound and x-ray).

question: Who provides legal help in Kakuma and how do I reach them?
answer: Free legal assistance in Kakuma is provided by the Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK). Call the toll-free line 0800 720 262 or the office line 0701 414 978. Legal aid clinics run at Compound 1, Field Post 1, Furaha Centre 2, Liz Ahua, the RCK office in Kakuma 4, and Kalobeyei Village 1. RCK also monitors detention at police stations and court processes.

question: How do I contact UNHCR in Kenya or Kakuma?
answer: Call the free UNHCR Kenya Help Line 1517, available 24/7 every day. You can email helpline.kenya@unhcr.org in any language you wish. If you are in Kakuma, you can also write to kenkaprt@unhcr.org. Operators can advise on procedures, your rights, and the services available in your area.
